questions.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(-2,0)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x).$ Which point must lie on $y=-f(x)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The transformation $y=-f(x)$ reflects the curve $y=f(x)$ in the $x$-axis.

First, notice that the point $P(-2,0)$ lies on the $x$-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected to itself.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217907/assets/808bdc6ebdad390ce7bec9f2ce43dacefe8a120c6b86c48c5740e02228867b63.png)

We conclude that the point  $(-2,0)$  must lie on the graph of $y=-f(x).$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The transformation $y=-f(x)$ reflects the curve $y=f(x)$ in the $x$-axis.

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
The graph of $y=f(x)$ shown below. How can we plot the graph of $y=-f(x)$?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217907/assets/5bab57ba6ac7cd9b0ea80287457ddc7ee50cadf2580a84a802fa039bbca27e1a.png)

As usual, It's helpful to first find a few points on the graph of $y=-f(x)$. You can use the points on the graph of $y=f(x)$ to identify corresponding points on the graph of $y=-f(x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Points on }y=f(x) & \text{ Points on }y=-f(x) \\ (-1,2) & (-1,-2) \\ (0,-1) & (0,1) \\ (2,0) & (2,0) \\ (3,4) & (3,-4)\end{aligned}
$$

For each point on the graph of $y=f(x)$ there is a point on the graph of $y=-f(x)$ with the *same* $x$-value and the *opposite* $y$-value. 

Let's plot our new points, and draw $y=-f(x)$.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217907/assets/5a1e6c5a95dff6b8e1f7eba5de197ba61f0ae64a94db2eeb57fc6cd23661f877.png)

The graph of $y=-f(x)$ is a **reflection across the $x$-axis** of the graph of $y=f(x)$.
